import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Filter for significant features (p < 0.1)
    sig_ids = [fid for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids) 
               if abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, i], feats.x[feats.y==0, i]).statistic) > 1.645]
    
    if not sig_ids:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Build correlation matrix for significant features
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in sig_ids]].T)
    corr_matrix = np.abs(corr_matrix)
    
    # Find clusters of highly correlated features (|r| >= 0.6)
    clusters = []
    visited = set()
    
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(sig_ids):
        if i in visited:
            continue
        cluster = {fid1}
        visited.add(i)
        
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(sig_ids[i+1:], i+1):
            if j in visited and corr_matrix[i,j] >= 0.6:
                cluster.add(fid2)
                visited.add(j)
                
        if len(cluster) > 1:
            clusters.append(list(cluster))
    
    # For each cluster, select the most significant feature (highest t-stat)
    representative_features = []
    for cluster in clusters:
        t_stats = [abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(fid)], 
                                      feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(fid)]).statistic) 
                   for fid in cluster]
        best_fid = cluster[np.argmax(t_stats)]
        representative_features.append(best_fid)
    
    # Select top features by t-statistic (excluding clustered ones)
    all_sig = [(fid, abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(fid)], 
                                         feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(fid)]).statistic)) 
               for fid in sig_ids if fid not in representative_features]
    all_sig.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    
    # Choose drivers based on strongest correlations, max 4 due to checker constraint
    drivers = [fid for fid, _ in all_sig[:4]]  # Limited to 4 drivers
    
    # Add representative features from clusters to drivers if space allows
    for fid in representative_features:
        if len(drivers) < 4 and fid not in drivers:
            drivers.append(fid)
    
    # Build columns and products
    columns = [fid for fid in sig_ids if fid not in drivers]
    
    # Check for interactions between top features
    products = []
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(drivers):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(drivers[i+1:], i+1):
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid1)], 
                               feats.x[:, feats.column(fid2)])[0,1]) > 0.6:
                products.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Create weighted loading based on effect sizes
    loadings = {}
    for fid in drivers:
        t_stat = stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(fid)], 
                                feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(fid)]).statistic
        loadings[fid] = abs(t_stat)
    
    # Normalize loadings
    total = sum(loadings.values())
    if total > 0:
        for k in loadings:
            loadings[k] /= total
    
    return Design(drivers=tuple(drivers), columns=tuple(columns), products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
